Yes: the closest matches are GNNs used as lightweight proxies for SDP relaxations. One paper studies GNNs as surrogates for linear SDPs, showing standard GNNs fail while a more expressive architecture can recover SDP solutions and warm-start a solver [1]. Another focuses on Max-Cut, proposing a GNN that directly serves as a principled proxy for SDP solvers, predicting primal- and dual-feasible SDP solutions and plugging into branch-and-bound [2].

If you want a general SDP-proxy result, [1] is broader; if you want an exact optimization use case with feasibility guarantees, [2] is more specialized to Max-Cut.
